summary: Standard L-4 cabin built by the Forest Service in 1934 on Cottonwood Point in Idaho's Challis forest; abandoned in 1946 and registered in 2026.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1946; no source confirms the cabin still stands, so the record's 'standing' is unverified.

access.note: Hike-in site inside the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness on Forest Service land. The level is inferred from the wilderness and hike-in notes; no source states an access rule.

visit.trail_note: Listed as hike-in by Idaho Fire Lookouts; the sources give no route, distance or road to the summit.

events.note: Standard L-4 cabin built by the U.S. Forest Service on the minor west summit of Cottonwood Point
Abandoned; no longer serves as an active fire tower
Registered June 28, 2026 as US 1828, ID 165, nominated by PJ Smith

corrections.why: The NHLR and firelookout.com entries say the cabin was abandoned in 1946 and no longer serves as an active fire tower. None of the sources says the cabin still stands.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 8,975 ft (2,736 m) and Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 8976 ft. The difference is one foot, so the record's 2735.6 m is kept.
Cottonwood Point is also the name of a 1937 pole-tower lookout in Bonner County, in a different part of Idaho. That site is not this lookout and is not used in the story.

notes_for_editor: Only four sources, all short. Nothing confirms whether the cabin still stands, so the record's 'standing' is not supported. The access level 'public' is inferred from the wilderness hike-in note. Source 4 covers a different Cottonwood Point in Bonner County and is used only to prevent confusion. Staffing is recorded as not staffed since 1946, based on the abandonment notes. Idaho Fire Lookouts has no staffing history for this site.
